liner.body_md:
## Setlist highlights

- **I need some Coke..." and "There will be a slight pause..." stage talk**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **One Kind Favor**: rare: 8 archived performances [15]
- **You See A Broken Heart**: rare: 4 archived performances [15]
- **PA and "tasting" and tuning stage talk**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **Just Bearly" PA stage talk**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **Heads Up**: rare: 3 archived performances [15]
- **How's the PA now" stage talk**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]
- **take a break" and "ice cream" stage talk**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [15]

## The recordings

- **gd66-03-19.sbd.scotton.81951.sbeok.flac** (recommended): soundboard; 17 songs; 67 min; rated 3.33/5 by 12 [1]
- **gd1966-03-19.153760.scotton.sirmick.remaster.flac16**: soundboard; 12 songs; 67 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer works in the Carthay Studios building, now known as Hi-Point Studios [5]
- Reviewer was born on 3-19-66, during this Grateful Dead performance [6]
- Neighbor attended the acid test; handbills confirm a show occurred on 3-19 [7]
- Reviewer and cousin Bob attended their first Grateful Dead show at age sixteen [8]
- Carthay Studios was located on Pico Blvd, identifying this as the Pico Acid Test [11]
- Reviewer questions if the ice cream mention refers to the Danish Center or outside the studio [13]
- The Acid Test moved from UCLA to Carthay Studios at the last minute [2]
- Weir's voice is slightly off-key in this recording, matching the 3/12 tape [9]
- The last riff on Viola is distinct, suggesting this is the 3/12 performance [10]
- Bobby comes in before Midnight Hour, confirming the 3/12 setlist [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd66-03-19.sbd.scotton.81951.sbeok.flac**: taped by Seed provided by Paul Scotton; transferred by Tracking by Ihor Slabicky; source: MSR>R>D>CDR>EAC>CDWav>Flac [1]. Also: Paul Scotton provided the tape, which David Lemieux later identified as 3/12/66; This is a nearly-complete, Bear-recorded set from the LA Pico test; Deadlists consensus identifies the tape as 3/12/66, though it arrived labeled 3/19/66 [1][4][12]
- **gd1966-03-19.153760.scotton.sirmick.remaster.flac16**: transferred by This is a remaster of shn id 81951 by SIRMick; source: Soundboard - provided by Paul Scotton (MSR > R > D > CDR > EAC > CD Wave > Flac) [2]
